observations: Photo 0 shows a cardboard box printed 'Nikon D750' with a Nikkor lens box beside it and a gimbal/stabilizer product image on another box.
Photo 1 shows the opened D750 box containing only paper manuals labeled 'Nikon D750 User's Manual', no camera body visible.
Photo 2 shows bubble-wrapped items inside a box; the wrapped shapes could be a lens hood or small lens, not clearly a camera body.
No camera body, LCD screen, lens mount, or serial plate is visible in any photo.
Seller's text claims 'Nikon D750 Body' then says 'The model is D850', a direct contradiction in the listing itself.

claims.claim: American used Nikon D750 Body, clean and pure as new
claims.evidence: Photo 0 and photo 1 show D750 packaging, but seller's own text later states 'The model is D850', a self-contradiction; no camera body is visible in any photo to confirm either model or condition.
No power-on, screen, shutter count, or video proof shown; only closed/bubble-wrapped boxes are visible.

risks.risk: Model mismatch between box/manual (D750) and seller's stated model (D850) suggests wrong item, mislabeled stock photos, or an attempt to pass off a cheaper body as a pricier one.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the camera body itself showing the model name on the front/top plate and the serial number.
risks.if_unproven: priced at the lower/less certain of the two claimed models, or treated as unidentified body risk

risks.risk: No actual camera body is shown in any photo, only boxes and bubble wrap; this is a known pattern for empty-box or stock-photo listings.
risks.proof: Photo of the unwrapped camera body powered on, showing lens mount, shutter count on screen, and serial number matching the box.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / item not confirmed present

risks.risk: Shutter count and sensor/screen condition cannot be assessed from box photos.
risks.proof: Photo of LCD screen showing shutter count via menu, plus a photo of the sensor and top/rear body for wear.
risks.if_unproven: priced as heavy-use/unknown condition, worst case

risks.risk: 'American used' origin and import/warranty status is an unverifiable claim.
risks.proof: Receipt, import sticker, or US retailer box sticker with serial number visible.

proof_requests: Photo of the actual camera body (not box) showing the model name plate on the front and the serial number.
Photo of the LCD screen displaying shutter actuation count.
Live photo/video of the camera powering on with lens attached, showing autofocus and shutter firing.
Clarification from seller resolving the D750 vs D850 discrepancy, matching serial number on box and body.
response.reason: The listing text itself contradicts the model (D750 box/manual vs. stated D850), and no camera body is shown in any photo—only sealed boxes and bubble wrap—matching a common empty-box or bait-and-switch scam pattern.
